theory_title: Working out where you actually stand
theory_content: Divide what you did not spend by what you took home. Under 10% means any shock becomes debt. Between 10 and 20% is a normal starting point. Above 30% and the date of financial independence starts moving in years rather than months. Calculate it from a real month, not an intended one — the gap between those two numbers is the whole problem.

Housing, transport and food are usually 60-70% of spending. A ₹5,000 reduction in rent is worth more than every subscription you could cancel, and it recurs without any further willpower. Most budgeting advice attacks small discretionary items because they are easy to name, not because they are where the money is.

theory_title: Budgeting when the month is not the unit
theory_content: For freelance or commission income, budget against your lowest three months of the past year, not the average. Route everything into one account, pay yourself a fixed "salary" from it, and let the surplus accumulate in good months to cover thin ones. Treating a good month as the new normal is the standard failure.

theory_title: Twenty minutes a month is enough
theory_content: You do not need to record every transaction forever. Track closely for one month to find out where the money actually goes, fix the two categories that surprised you, then review monthly against those. Continuous detailed tracking is what people abandon; a monthly review is what they keep.
